title: Availability Classification and Restoration SOP
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines a single, pragmatic standard operating procedure (SOP) for classifying availability incidents, restoring service, and coordinating communications. It consolidates triage steps, restoration runbooks, status page templates, postmortem requirements, on-call rotation responsibilities, and a repeatable game-day exercise plan.

Scope: Applies to Redwood Inference public API endpoints, dedicated tenant ingress, and the control plane used by Private deployments. Does NOT replace model-serving specific runbooks (see related runbooks in eng-serving-runtime).

Definitions and Severity Classification

1) Severity levels (availability-focused)
   - Sev-1 (Critical): Global or multi-region service outage causing API request failure for >50% of production requests or blocking all reads/writes for a paid customer. Objective: restore within 60 minutes or follow escalation policy.
   - Sev-2 (High): Significant degradation (latency > 3x SLO or 50–80% error rate) affecting multiple customers or a single enterprise customer with dedicated capacity. Objective: interim mitigation within 4 hours.
   - Sev-3 (Medium): Partial degradation localized to a region, single service, or non-blocking errors (e.g., 10–30% increased error rate). Objective: remediation within 48 hours.
   - Sev-4 (Low): Operational anomalies, alerts without customer impact, or routine maintenance tasks. Objective: address in normal sprint cycle.

SLOs and Alert Thresholds (excerpt)

| Component | 99th latency | Error rate alert | SLO target |
|-----------|-------------:|-----------------:|-----------:|
| Public API (text-generation) | 600ms | >5% over 5m | 99.9% availability monthly |
| Embeddings endpoint | 400ms | >3% over 5m | 99.95% availability monthly |
| Control plane (auth/keys) | 200ms | >1% over 5m | 99.99% availability monthly |

Ownership and Roles

- Incident Commander (IC): First responder from engineering-oncall who takes coordination lead for the active incident.
- Service Owner: Team that owns the failing service (e.g., runtime-serving, routing, queue-proxy).
- Communications Lead: Eng-SRE or Customer Success rep who drafts customer-facing messages.
- Pager: The on-call engineer(s) for the implicated service.
- Exec Liaison: Senior engineering manager notified for Sev-1 and prolonged Sev-2 incidents.

Triage Matrix (quick guide)

1) Initial detection (automated alert, pager, or customer report)
   - Validate: Confirm alert signal (check metrics, logs, recent deploys).
   - Classify: Use error footprint + business impact to assign severity.
   - IC assigned: Pager duty system auto-assigns; if unclear, the first responder becomes IC for first 15 minutes.

2) If Sev-1 or unresolved after 15 minutes: escalate to on-call SRE lead and notify Exec Liaison.

Standard Restoration Procedure (step-by-step)

A) Containment (first 10–30 minutes)
   1. Apply temporary traffic routing: divert traffic to fallback model variant or region. CLI example:

   # Toggle routing policy to fallback pool
   redwoodctl routes set --service public-api --policy fallback-pool

   2. Disable autoscale policies that may worsen instability.
   3. If root cause unknown, enable verbose trace sampling for 5–10 minutes and capture core dumps/heap profiles.

B) Remediation (30–180 minutes)
   1. Identify root component: check metrics dashboards (latency, error rate, queue depth), recent deploys, config changes, and infra events.
   2. If a recent deploy is suspected, perform a fast rollback:

   # Roll back to previous model-served revision
   redwoodctl deploy rollback --service runtime-serving --to-revision v2025-01-10-rc3

   3. Apply config toggles (e.g., reduce batch size, force synchronous KV cache bypass) per component runbooks. See runbook links in "Runbook mapping" below.

C) Recovery validation (post-remediation)
   1. Run synthetic health checks across regions and client SDKs.
   2. Confirm ticketing and monitoring show metrics returning to baseline for two consecutive 5-minute intervals.
   3. If service remains degraded, escalate to engineering incident review for next actions (hotfix/patch or capacity change).

Communications and Status Page Templates

Internal status updates cadence (IC responsibility):
- T+15m: Short summary of what is known + next 30m plan (post to #incidents slack and update internal status doc).
- T+60m: Detailed update with mitigations applied and customer impact estimate.
- T+240m: Restoration confirmation + next steps and ETA for full remediation.
- Post-incident: Postmortem link + summary (within 72 hours).

Public status page template (JSON snippet for status pipeline)

{
  "status": "degraded_performance",
  "components": ["public-api", "embeddings"],
  "impact": "Some customers are experiencing increased latency and errors when calling the text-generation and embeddings endpoints.",
  "updates": [
    {"time": "2025-02-12T14:12:00Z", "message": "Identified elevated error rates; applying routing fallback to reduce customer impact."},
    {"time": "2025-02-12T15:05:00Z", "message": "Traffic routing applied. Observing reduced error rates; monitoring for stabilization."}
  ]
}

Customer email template (short)

Subject: Service impact update — Redwood API (partial degradation)

Hello,

We are investigating an issue impacting text-generation and embeddings. Some requests may fail or experience higher latency. We have implemented traffic fallback to reduce customer impact and are actively monitoring. We will provide a follow-up update by 15:05 UTC.

If you are seeing a critical production impact, reply to this message and we will prioritize a direct escalation.

— Redwood Inference Support

Postmortem and RCA Requirements

- Timeline: Include exact times for detection, mitigation steps, and full restoration.
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence (logs, traces, config diffs).
- Contributing factors and corrective actions with owners and due dates.
- Severity validation against classification matrix.
- Lessons learned and detection improvement tasks (alerts, dashboards).
- Publish draft within 72 hours (IC) and final postmortem with action items closed or scheduled within 30 days.

On-call Rotations and Handoff Expectations

- Primary on-call rotation: team-managed weekly schedule. Engineers should ensure runbook access and up-to-date contact info in PagerDuty.
- Handoff checklist (on shift start/end):
   1. Review active incidents and oncall board.
   2. Confirm access to runbook links and escalation contacts.
   3. Note any scheduled maintenance and expected noisy alerts.
- Escalation triggers: failure to acknowledge pager in 5 minutes, unresolved Sev-1 after 15 minutes.

Game-day exercise plan (quarterly)

Objective: Validate the end-to-end incident workflow, including detection, routing fallbacks, public communications, and postmortem cadence.

Exercise cadence and roles:
- Frequency: Quarterly (every 3 months).
- Duration: 90 minutes + 30 minutes debrief.
- Participants: On-call engineer, Eng-SRE lead, Service Owner, CS Communications Lead.

Sample scenario (45-minute timeline):
1) Inject simulated increased error rate in staging which mimics a regression from a recent deploy.
2) On-call must detect via alert, assign IC, and execute containment (traffic shift) within 20 minutes.
3) Communications Lead publishes a status page update and internal incident note.
4) Team performs rollback in staging and validates recovery.
5) Debrief covers timeline, missed alerts, and improvement items.

Runbook governance and health checks

- Every runbook referenced here must be reviewed at least once per quarter by the Service Owner.
- Runbook validation checklist: accuracy of commands, recent owner contact, and a working verification command or synthetic check.

Escalation Matrix (condensed)

| Trigger | Primary | Escalate after | Next | Exec notify |
|--------:|:--------|:--------------:|:-----|:-----------:|
| Pager unacked | On-call | 5 min | Team lead | No |
| Sev-1 unresolved | IC | 15 min | SRE Lead | Yes (phone) |
| Customer P1 reported | CS Lead | immediate | IC + SRE Lead | Yes |

Appendix: Useful CLI snippets and artifacts to capture

- redwoodctl logs tail --service runtime-serving --since 10m --level error
- Capture core dumps: /var/crash/core-<pid>.tgz
- Snapshot of queue depth: redwoodctl metrics query --name queue_depth --window 5m

Document maintenance

Owner: Eng-SRE.
Review cadence: annually for classification thresholds; quarterly for runbook links and playbook commands.
